item.text:
The sign-in starts in [login-form.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx). `LoginForm` reads the email, password and “Keep me signed in” checkbox and runs `loginSchema.safeParse` from [auth.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/schemas/auth.ts). This client-side check provides field errors; the server checks the input again. On success, the form calls `loginAction`.

In [login.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/actions/auth/login.ts), `loginAction` validates the input again and calls `consumeRateLimit` against the anonymous login bucket. It then calls `login` in [auth-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/server/services/auth-service.ts), which also consumes that login rate limit before checking credentials. The service uses `findUserByEmail` and `findPasswordHash` in [user-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts); the email lookup lowercases the address. `verifyPassword` in [hash.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/lib/hash.ts) derives a scrypt key from the supplied password and stored salt, then compares it with the stored key using a timing-safe comparison. An unknown user, missing hash or incorrect password produces the same credential error.

After a match, `login` calls `createSessionToken` in [session-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/server/services/session-service.ts). It generates a random 32-byte, base64url token and a 30-day expiry. `createSession` in [session-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/server/repositories/session-repository.ts) stores a new session row with the user ID, a SHA-256 **hash** of the token, expiry, timestamps and a null `activeOrgId`. The raw token is returned to the action, not stored in that row.

`loginAction` immediately calls `resolveSession` with the raw token to obtain a `SessionPrincipal`, then `setSessionCookie` in [session.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/lib/session.ts) hands the raw token to the browser as the `taskflow_session` cookie. The cookie is HTTP-only, `SameSite=Lax`, scoped to `/`, secure in production, and expires with the session. The action returns the principal—user ID, email, active organization ID and expiry—to the form. Although the checkbox is parsed, the login and session creation code does not use `rememberMe` to change the lifetime.

On success, `LoginForm` navigates to its `next` prop. [The login page](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx) supplies that destination using `safeDestination`, defaulting to `/orgs`, and redirects an already signed-in visitor there too. At [the organization chooser](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/app/(dashboard)/orgs/page.tsx), `Page` lists the principal’s organizations: it redirects directly when there is one and otherwise presents a choice.

For a later protected request, `proxy` in [proxy.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/proxy.ts) first checks only whether the cookie has a value. If absent, it redirects to login with the requested path as `next`; a present cookie alone does not establish a valid session. The authenticated [dashboard layout](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx) calls `getSessionPrincipal` and redirects to login if it returns null.

`getSessionPrincipal` reads the cookie through `getSessionToken` and calls `resolveSession`. That function hashes the presented token and calls `findSessionByTokenHash`, which joins the session to its user, rejects an unknown or expired row, and constructs the principal. `getSessionPrincipal` also checks the principal’s expiry against the current time. Thus the browser supplies the bearer token on later requests, while the database lookup and expiry determine whether it still identifies a signed-in user.

The principal identifies a user but does not contain a workspace role. In the [organization layout](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx), the app resolves the organization from the URL and calls `resolveActorForOrg(principal, orgSlug)`. That function looks up the organization and the user’s membership, requires an **active** membership, and builds an `Actor` containing `userId`, `orgId` and the membership’s `role`. It calls `assertOrgScope` and updates the member’s last-seen time. The layout returns a 404 for a missing organization or inaccessible membership and checks the actor’s scope again.

The layout then builds an organization-specific feature-flag snapshot and passes the actor, flags and workspace data through `OrgProvider` and `DashboardShell` to [AppSidebar](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/components/domain/nav/app-sidebar.tsx). `AppSidebar` calls `visibleNav` in [nav.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/config/nav.ts), which filters navigation items by their flags and by `can`. In [permissions.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/lib/permissions.ts), `can` delegates to `explain`: it checks organization scope, any staff bypass, the action’s minimum role and applicable ownership grants. For example, billing navigation requires the owner role, while flag management requires admin.

Workspace pages can independently obtain the same authorization context through `loadTenantContext` in [tenant-context.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/_lib/tenant-context.ts), which uses `getActor` in [actor.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/331830fa-b06a-4dc8-8df3-0b22fa85befc/src/lib/actor.ts), asserts organization scope and builds the flag snapshot. Server-side actions and services can then authorize operations against the scoped actor rather than relying on which sidebar links were shown.
